description:
Redwood Inference’s “Private observability minimum pack” project delivers a baseline, supported observability bundle for Redwood Private installs (VPC and on-prem), ensuring customers and Redwood Support/SRE can reliably monitor health, performance, and correctness without bespoke setup. The goal is to standardize a minimum set of dashboards, alerts, and log pipelines that ship with the private installer/Helm charts and are validated in reference environments.

Goals:
- Provide a default, turnkey observability stack integration for Private installs: core metrics, logs, and (where feasible) traces.
- Ship a curated set of “minimum supported” Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules that cover the highest-impact failure modes for inference (latency, error rate, saturation, GPU/CPU/memory pressure, queueing/backpressure, restart loops, storage pressure).
- Define and implement a supported log pipeline for control plane + data plane components (structured logs, retention defaults, and safe redaction guidance), with export options suitable for private environments (e.g., SIEM/Splunk/ELK/Loki/OTLP endpoints).
- Produce operational runbooks and troubleshooting playbooks for day-2 operations and Support escalations.

Scope:
- In-scope components: private control plane services, API gateway, routing/policy engine, serving runtime pods, model registry integration points, and installer/upgrade controller.
- Observability artifacts: Prometheus rules/recording rules, Grafana dashboards, log collection/forwarding configuration, documentation, and validation test plan.
- Deployment surfaces: Helm charts and the private installer (including offline/on-prem packaging constraints such as image mirroring and air-gapped upgrades).

Out of scope (v1):
- Full enterprise “observability premium” features (long retention, multi-cluster federation, advanced tracing with full sampling controls, customer-specific dashboard customization).
- Building a new in-house SIEM; instead provide documented export integrations.

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments) for requirements, packaging/positioning, and defining “supported minimum.”
- Engineering (Platform/Telemetry/Private Deployments): Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Diego Santos.
- SRE/Observability: Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Rafael Mendes.
- Solutions Engineering / PS: Markus Klein, Colin O’Donnell, Fatima Noor, Bruno Silva for customer constraints and reference architectures.
- Security & Compliance: review log content, retention defaults, and audit logging interactions.

Phases & timeline (typical):
1) Requirements & inventory (2–3 weeks): audit current Private deployments, top incidents/support cases, define minimum signals and SLO-aligned alerts.
2) Design & standards alignment (2 weeks): decide on dashboard taxonomy, metric naming/cardinality constraints, alert philosophy, and supported export paths.
3) Implementation (4–6 weeks): add/normalize metrics, ship dashboards/alerts in `observability-pack` + wire into `redwood-helm-charts` and `redwood-private-installer`; implement log pipeline defaults.
4) Validation (2–3 weeks): run in VPC and on-prem-like environments; failure-injection checks; upgrade/rollback verification.
5) Enablement & launch (1–2 weeks): publish Confluence docs/runbooks, provide Support playbooks, and complete release notes.

Constraints:
- Private/on-prem environments may be air-gapped; all images and dashboards must be packaged and versioned.
- Must avoid leaking secrets/PII in logs; provide redaction guidance and safe defaults.
- Metrics cardinality must be bounded to protect customer clusters.
- Must support upgrades/rollbacks without breaking dashboards/alerts (backward-compatible metric names or documented migrations).

files.description: Published overview of the minimum pack: what’s included (dashboards, alerts, logs), supported environments (VPC/on-prem), versioning strategy, and how it gets installed via Helm/installer.
On-prem packaging guidance for air-gapped installs: image mirroring list, dashboard/rule artifacts, checksum/signing expectations, and upgrade compatibility notes.
Day-2 operations playbook: verifying signals after install/upgrade, common failure modes (Prometheus scrape issues, Grafana datasource auth), and escalation paths.
Catalog of dashboards included in v1: per-service views, golden signals, GPU fleet panels, queueing/batching panels, and links to the owning components/teams.
SLO recommendations for Private installs (API availability, p95/p99 latency, error rates) and how the minimum pack alerting maps to these SLOs.
Standards doc defining required metrics, naming conventions, label cardinality constraints, alert severity taxonomy, and recording rules expected for Private.
Infra runbook for running Prometheus/Grafana in customer clusters: sizing guidelines, storage/retention defaults, and troubleshooting scrape/TSDB issues.
Security-oriented doc describing what gets logged where, how audit logs relate to operational logs, recommended retention, and redaction guidance.
Support-facing list of known issues and workarounds for the minimum pack (dashboards empty, alerts noisy, log forwarder backpressure) with references to runbooks.
PRD-style requirements: target personas (customer platform team, Redwood Support), must-have dashboards/alerts/log exports, non-goals, and acceptance criteria.
ADR documenting scope decisions (what’s in/out), dependency on Prometheus/Grafana vs alternatives, and how export integrations are handled.
ADR covering log pipeline defaults: collector choice, structured logging format, redaction approach, and supported sinks (Loki/ELK/Splunk/OTLP).
Working kickoff notes: initial goals, candidate dashboards/alerts list, owners, and early risks (air-gapped constraints, cardinality).
Rough dashboard outlines and panel lists (golden signals, GPU panels, queue depth), including open questions and naming proposals.
Spreadsheet-like analysis of proposed alert rules, thresholds, and expected noise; includes mapping to Sev levels and paging policy suggestions.
Matrix of supported log export targets by environment (VPC/on-prem), auth methods, and required customer prerequisites.
Draft sizing guidance (CPU/mem/storage) for Prometheus/Grafana/log collector based on request volume and retention targets.
Launch brief draft: messaging for ‘supported’ installs, support readiness checklist, release timing, and upgrade notes.
Validation plan for on-prem/air-gapped: artifact bundle verification, simulated upgrade/rollback, and failure injection checks.
List of gaps between Hosted/Dedicated console observability and what’s feasible in Private; prioritization notes for future iterations.
PM ticket defining the ‘minimum supported’ observability pack for Private, with acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
Eng ticket to inventory existing metrics/dashboards used in hosted environments and identify what can be shipped to Private.
Task to normalize metric names/labels, reduce cardinality, and document backwards-compatibility/migrations.
Add recording rules for request rate, error rate, latency, saturation, and queue metrics suitable for dashboards/alerts.
Build the primary runtime dashboard for Private installs (latency, token throughput, batching, KV cache, GPU utilization).
Dashboard for control plane services (config/policy service health, API gateway, auth/RBAC integration points).
Define Prometheus alert rules for latency SLO burn and availability signals; align severities with paging policy.
Alert rules for GPU saturation, OOM kills, restart loops, and resource pressure in inference workloads.
Implement baseline log collector config (structured logs parsing, batching/backpressure) and safe defaults.
Add documented and tested configuration for exporting logs to Splunk HEC in Private environments.
Add documented and tested configuration for exporting logs to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.
Wire dashboards/rules/log configs into `redwood-helm-charts` with versioned values and sane defaults.
Add preflight checks for storage class, scrape targets, network policies, and resource requests for the observability components.
Ensure offline bundle contains the observability artifacts and validate install without internet access.
Plan and implement upgrade/rollback-safe migrations when dashboards or metric names change.
Automated smoke tests verifying Prometheus scrapes, dashboards render, and alerts fire under injected failures.
Security review task for ensuring logs don’t include secrets/PII, and that retention defaults are compliant.
Write Confluence runbooks and support playbooks; link to known-issues and escalation procedures.
GA readiness ticket: validations complete, support enablement done, release notes drafted, and ownership clarified.
PR adding a versioned bundle of Grafana dashboards for Private minimum pack (runtime + control plane + infra panels).
PR introducing baseline alert rules and recording rules; includes threshold rationale and runbook links.
PR adding GPU/resource pressure alerts tailored for inference pods; includes noise tuning notes.
PR wiring dashboards/alerts into Helm chart values, adding toggles for customers to enable/disable exporters and set retention.
PR adding installer checks (storage/network/resources) and post-install validation steps that confirm scrapes and dashboards.
PR ensuring air-gapped bundle includes dashboards/rules/log configs and updating bundle manifest.
PR standardizing service metrics and reducing cardinality (e.g., route/model labels) to be safe for customer Prometheus.
PR adding/aligning structured log fields (request_id, tenant_id hash, model, route) and redaction safeguards.
PR adding a smoke-test harness that deploys a minimal private cluster and asserts observability signals show up.
PR updating internal/external docs: install steps, dashboard catalog, alert meanings, and export configuration examples.
Thread coordinating which dashboards are ‘must-have’ vs ‘nice-to-have’, with quick links to panels and owners.
Thread discussing high-cardinality labels (model, tenant, route) and an agreed plan to cap/aggregate for Private.
Thread aligning alert severities with paging policy and defining what is page-worthy vs ticket-only in Private.
Thread with back-and-forth on TSDB sizing, retention defaults, and recommended PVC sizes for typical private footprints.
Thread brainstorming installer preflight checks for observability components and what failures should be hard-blocking.
Thread with Security reviewing log fields, redaction approach, and retention guidance; includes questions about request payload logging.
Support coordination thread for a private customer where dashboards went blank after an upgrade; links to Jira and proposed workaround.
Incident-style thread capturing triage of scrape failures caused by tightened NetworkPolicies in a customer cluster.
Thread identifying missing artifacts in the offline bundle and coordinating a hotfix in the private installer.
Thread reviewing early alert noise in staging, adjusting thresholds, and deciding which alerts are disabled by default.
Thread debugging log forwarder backpressure (buffer limits, retry) and whether to prioritize durability vs resource usage.
Thread debating whether OTLP export is required for v1 or if documented Splunk/ELK exporters are sufficient.
Product/Eng thread aligning on what ‘supported’ means, and what gets deferred to future releases.
Release coordination thread for branching/backport strategy and the required docs/runbooks before tagging.
Oncall feedback thread requesting runbook URLs and ‘what to do first’ steps embedded directly in alert annotations.
Customer support ticket: Private install completed but Grafana shows no Redwood dashboards; includes environment details, logs, and resolution steps.
Ticket about noisy alerts post-upgrade (CPU/memory thresholds too tight); includes tuning recommendations and linked PR for rule changes.
Ticket diagnosing Splunk HEC auth errors for log export; includes config snippets, customer constraints, and workaround.
Internal support ticket for CI failures in the private observability smoke-test pipeline; includes logs and assignment to infra/SRE.
Transcript of a technical deep dive with an enterprise prospect about Private observability requirements (SIEM exports, air-gapped constraints, alerting expectations).
Transcript of a security review call focused on logging content, retention, audit logs vs operational logs, and export controls for Private deployments.
Email thread between Product (Private) and Eng/SRE managers aligning on requirements, definition of ‘supported,’ and launch timeline; includes doc links and action items.
Sales/SE email thread answering an enterprise customer’s questions about dashboards/alerts, log export options, and air-gapped packaging; includes attachments (draft architecture PDF).
Leadership thread requesting resourcing approval and confirming cross-team owners (Telemetry, SRE, Private Deployments) for the minimum pack delivery.
